subject: Transient microburst attribution — request for uptime reweighting
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Skylark Health NOC <noc@skylarkhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-26T06:45:00-07:00
Subject: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

On Oct 26 between about 06:14-06:23 PT we observed a spike of 502/504 responses for our EU and US customers that coincided with a planned maintenance window announced by TransitCo (notice attached). Approximately 9 minutes of traffic saw 40-60% error rates for a subset of our endpoints.

We understand third-party maintenance can cause transit blips, but our contract with Redwood shows a single aggregated availability % for the period and the current invoice indicates no credit. Can you confirm whether TransitCo-maintenance should be excluded or if this counts as a partial degradation attributable to Redwood?

Attached: skylark_path_logs_oct26.zip (packet traces + app logs). We can share a pcap extract if helpful.

Request: a formal recount of uptime for Oct 26, and an interim credit while you apportion responsibility.

Thanks,
Eleanor Park
Head of Infrastructure
Skylark Health
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-26T07:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Thanks for the detailed logs, Eleanor — we got them. I pulled a quick probe run and see the same short-duration spike.

Im looping in Marissa (SRE/investigations) and Ben (account lead) to get a formal apportionment and credit proposal. Can you confirm whether Skylark saw the same error profile in both US and EU backends or was EU-only worse? Also, please paste the TransitCo maintenance notice URL (we saw a bulletin but need the ticket id).

Well follow up with an initial assessment within 24 hours.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-27T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Eleanor — thanks for the packet captures. Preliminary analysis from our edge probes shows a 9-minute elevated error window starting 2027-10-26T06:14:20-07:00. Impact summary:

- Affected POPs: 2 of 5 in the US region (SFO, LAX) and 1 of 3 in EU (AMS) during overlapping minutes.
- Error profile: elevated 5xx rate (~45% on average) for a 9-minute span, with traffic reroutes evident in BGP logs.
- Root cause indicators: TransitCo announced a rolling fabric maintenance that produced temporary path flaps; TransitCo support ticket 45218 (link below) matches the window.

Given the partial nature (not full-path outage) and the fact that only a subset of POPs were affected, our usual approach is apportionment: we calculate Redwoods responsibility by weighting per-probe failure fraction and route ownership. Based on initial weighting, Redwoods share is ~40% responsibility for the minutes in question; TransitCo would be ~60%.

Proposed next steps:
1) We apply a provisional credit on the Nov invoice equivalent to 40% of the impacted minutes (we show ~9 minutes impacted across a multi-hour window).
2) We continue the joint investigation with TransitCo and Skylark to confirm cross-pop routing and finalize apportionment within 14 days.
3) If TransitCo formally confirms maintenance-as-planned that explains the path flaps, we will exclude the TransitCo maintenance interval from our uptime denominator for that event (standard third-party exception), subject to confirmation from TransitCo.

Attachments: probe-summary-20271026.csv, link to detailed logs: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cSKYLARK-logs

Please confirm youre ok with the provisional 40% credit while we finalize. If you have additional region-specific metrics that push the weighting toward TransitCo, share them and well update.

—Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Skylark Health NOC <noc@skylarkhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>, TransitCo Support <support@transitco.net>
Date: 2027-10-27T13:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Hi Marissa, Jonas,

Thanks for the prompt analysis. We can confirm the EU (AMS) customer-facing services saw a higher error rate and multiple reroutes to backup transit during the window; our metrics show the EU path experienced ~65% errors for 7 minutes, whereas US was ~35% averaged across the affected POPs.

TransitCo provided this maintenance notice: https://support.transitco.net/tickets/45218 (you also have the PDF attached). Our ask is to exclude the TransitCo maintenance window entirely from Redwoods SLA denominator for the purposes of the Oct billing period, since the primary causal factor appears to be TransitCo fabric changes.

If Redwood is unable to fully exclude, we request a clear apportionment calculation laid out in a one-page statement for our procurement team. Wed like the provisional credit reflected on the next invoice and a written letter we can attach to our records.

Regards,
Skylark NOC
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Skylark Health NOC <noc@skylarkhealth.com>, Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Eleanor / Skylark NOC — appreciate the details and the patience here. We want to resolve this cleanly. Proposed commercial compromise while the policy/apportionment paperwork is completed:

- One-off goodwill credit equivalent to 6 hours of service for the Oct invoice (we will apply as an invoice line item).
- Final apportionment statement to be delivered within 14 days after Redwoods deeper joint investigation with TransitCo; that will determine whether the TransitCo window is excluded or a shared-responsibility credit is applied.

If that approach works for you well get finance to prepare the credit and legal to draft a one-page apportionment summary you can attach to procurement. If you need the credit processed sooner for accounting cutoffs, tell us the amount and well prioritize.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@skylarkhealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Skylark Health NOC <noc@skylarkhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient microburst during TransitCo maintenance — request for uptime recount

Ben / team — that compromise works for Skylark. Thank you for moving quickly. Two asks:

1) Please confirm the invoice line item id for the 6-hour goodwill credit and an expected posting date.
2) Please send the one-page apportionment summary and a short formal letter we can share with procurement stating the provisional credit was applied pending final apportionment.

Well share any final TransitCo confirmation if/when we receive it. Thanks again — appreciate the partnership on this.

Best,
Eleanor
Head of Infrastructure, Skylark Health
